summary.short: Malaysia's Online Safety Act 2025 requires licensed applications and content applications service providers to mitigate exposure to harmful content, protect child users, offer reporting mechanisms and submit Online Safety Plans, enforced by the Communications and Multimedia Commission. It applies from a date set by ministerial notification.
summary.long: The Act covers applications services, content applications services and network services using internet access, excluding private messaging features, and reaches licensees outside Malaysia that provide such services in Malaysia. It creates an Online Safety Committee to advise the Communications and Multimedia Commission and an Online Safety Appeal Tribunal. Licensed applications and content applications service providers must implement code-specified measures against exposure to harmful content, issue user guidelines, provide user tools and reporting mechanisms, protect child users, make priority harmful content inaccessible, and prepare an Online Safety Plan. The Commission may issue written instructions, directions and notices of non-compliance; financial penalties for non-compliance with duties may not exceed RM10 million, and failing to comply with a written instruction or direction carries a fine of up to RM1 million plus daily fines. Secrecy breaches carry up to three months' imprisonment. The First Schedule lists harmful content categories and the Second Schedule defines priority harmful content. Commencement is set by ministerial notification.

notes: Entries are populated for relations and entities, so section_status is set to not_applicable for schema compliance only. Commencement is by Minister's notification in the Gazette (s.1(2)); the text gives no commencement date, so in-force status rests on the registry metadata. Many periods are left 'as may be prescribed' (ss.14, 17, 20-29, 81), so the regulations are needed for those deadlines. Section 4 defines 'user' only by reference to users of services of licensed providers, while s.24(1)(b) allows a user to report harmful content available elsewhere online; the text does not define 'user' for that case. Duties in Part III apply to licensed applications and content applications service providers; these classes are addressees of obligations, not named entities, and are not listed in entities. Private right of action: the Act neither creates nor excludes one for users; s.78-79 bar suits against the Committee, Tribunal, Commission, authorised officers and persons acting in good faith under Commission instructions (private_right_of_action left null).

obligations.summary: Licensed applications and content applications service providers must implement code-specified measures to mitigate user exposure to harmful content; they may use alternative measures if the Commission is satisfied. Measures must not unreasonably or disproportionately limit user expression (s.13(3)). Network service providers are named in s.25 and s.30, not here.

evidence.quote: shall implement the measures as specified in the code to mitigate the risk of users being exposed to harmful content.

obligations.summary: Issue guidelines to users describing the measures under s.13 and the terms of use; make the guidelines available on the service, clear, easily accessible and regularly updated (s.14(2)).

obligations.summary: Make available on the service sufficient tools and settings for users to manage their online safety, including tools to prevent or limit other users from identifying, locating or communicating with them.

obligations.summary: Make available a user assistance mechanism that is easily accessible and responsive at all times, for raising online safety concerns (including s.13 measures), obtaining information within the prescribed period, and making inquiries.

obligations.summary: Implement code-specified measures to ensure safe use of services by child users. Measures must include, for services likely accessed by children: preventing child access to suspected harmful content, limiting adult-to-child communication, limiting features that extend use by children, preventing adults viewing children's personal information, and controlling personalised recommendation systems (s.18(3)). Alternative measures are permitted on the Commission's satisfaction (s.18(2)).
obligations.applies_from: date to be appointed by the Minister under s.1(2)

evidence.quote: shall implement the measures as specified in the code to ensure safe use of their services by child users.
